name: Spotable
tagline: A hosted tool for saving, organizing and sharing curated spots on a map.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: The core of a saved-spots app is a database table with a latitude, a longitude, a few tags and a map tile layer, and an agent will hand you that in an afternoon. What takes longer is everything around it: decent place search, photos, a phone-shaped interface you actually reach for while standing on a sidewalk, and links that render nicely when you send a list to a friend. Geocoding and tiles mean a third-party key unless you enjoy running your own tile server, so the build is not fully self-contained. If the spots are for you, the DIY version is genuinely fine and probably faster to use. If you share lists with other people and want them to look good on someone else's phone, the gap is real.
coreLoopDIY: A local web app where you search or drop a pin, save it with tags and notes, and browse your spots on a map or in a filterable list.
requirements: A map tile source (OpenStreetMap raster tiles or a MapTiler key in .env)
Nominatim or similar for place search, rate limits respected
Somewhere to run it if you want it on your phone (a small VPS or Tailscale back to your laptop)
whatYouLose: A real mobile app with offline caching and location permission handled properly
Rich place data: hours, photos, ratings, addresses that stay correct
Pretty shared links and collaborative lists that non-technical friends can open
Import from Google Maps saved places and other existing collections
Someone else keeping the tile and geocoding bills and keys alive
moatNotes: The hard part is not the map, it is the place database behind the search box and the fact that it works on a phone in one thumb tap.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because a saved-spots tool lives or dies on friction. The moment you have to open a laptop, remember a local URL or wait for a self-hosted geocoder to answer, you stop saving spots and go back to screenshots in your camera roll. Paying gets you an app icon, a working search box wired to a real place database, and shareable links that do not require explaining what a port is. The DIY build wins if you are mostly curating deliberately at a desk, and loses if the whole point is capturing something in three seconds while walking past it.
notes: Details on this one are thin, so treat the pricing and feature read as unverified.
prompt:
Build a local-first personal saved-spots app called MySpots. Stack, no substitutions:
Next.js 15 with the App Router, TypeScript, Tailwind, SQLite via better-sqlite3, MapLibre GL JS for the map.
No accounts, no auth, no cloud services, no analytics, no telemetry. Single user on localhost.

Data model in SQLite, created by a migration script on first run:
spots(id, name, lat, lng, address, notes, tags, rating_int, visited_bool, created_at)
lists(id, name, created_at) and list_spots(list_id, spot_id) for many-to-many.

Screens:
1. Map view: MapLibre with OpenStreetMap raster tiles, markers for every spot, click a marker for a popup with name, tags and an edit link. Clicking empty map opens an 'add spot here' form prefilled with the clicked coordinates.
2. List view: table of all spots, text filter, tag filter chips, sort by name or created_at, toggle visited.
3. Spot detail and edit form: name, address, notes (markdown rendered on view), comma-separated tags, 1 to 5 rating, visited checkbox, delete with confirm.
4. Lists page: create a named list, add or remove spots, and a read-only view of a single list showing only its spots on the map.

Search: a search box that queries the Nominatim public API for a place name, shows up to 5 results, and saving one copies name, address, lat and lng into the spot. Debounce to one request per second, send a descriptive User-Agent, and cache results in memory for the session.

Import and export: a JSON export of all tables and a JSON import that upserts by id. Also accept a GeoJSON FeatureCollection of points on import.

Config: .env.local holds TILE_URL and optional MAPTILER_KEY. Default to plain OSM tiles if no key is set. Commit .env.example, never a real key.

Out of scope, do not build: mobile app, push notifications, photo uploads beyond a single image URL field, sharing, multi-user, offline mode.

Deliver a README with setup in three commands, plus a seed script that inserts five example spots so the map is not empty on first load.
